failure_modes: Treating every risk as failure to hold a shape and missing failures to add enough mass or information
Reading an exponential growth curve as a shape to hit rather than as a sign of shape deformation
Treating the three dimensions as independent objectives instead of interacting forces
gloss: Growth risk is the balance of controlling shape, adding mass and adding information
invariants: Adding mass or information for its own value reduces control of shape
A decision is a special case of organisation growth, not its general form
mechanism: Any growing organisation, from a gene to a firm, is steered along three interacting dimensions. Shape is the form or target being held, such as a plan, a blueprint or an objective. Mass is any investment of action, money or energy that scales the organisation. Information is what is added to it as it grows. A decision is one corner of this space: shape is frozen, then mass is added. Mass and information pursued for their own value loosen control of shape, so risk comes from a bad combination of the three for the conditions, not only from a wrong decision. Human practice favours shape control, while Nature adds information as it adds mass through {{meta_modularity}}.
